clue.text: Arrange most of great Mongolian assemblage

indicators.note: most of a phrase is all but its final letter, so the tail is dropped
to arrange things is to put them into a fresh order, so the remaining letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; its last letter goes

explanation.surface: An instruction to organise a vast Mongolian gathering, perhaps a horde on the steppe.
explanation.definitionFit: An agglomeration is a mass or cluster of things gathered together, which is what an assemblage is.

clue.text: Large bird making most of flock angry when flying

indicators.note: most of the word is everything except its final letter
letters that are flying are scattered through the air and land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written; its last letter goes
taken as written

explanation.surface: A big bird of prey upsets a flock of smaller birds as it swoops among them.
explanation.definitionFit: The gyrfalcon is the largest species of falcon, a big Arctic raptor.

clue.text: Actress shows endless skill

indicators.note: something endless has lost its ends, so the first and last letters are cut away

blocks.note: sleight is dexterity or skill, as in sleight of hand

explanation.surface: A performer displays boundless talent on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing both ends of SLEIGHT leaves LEIGH, as in Vivien Leigh.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivien Leigh was the British film star who played Scarlett O'Hara in Gone with the Wind.

clue.text: Rob's up for Trivial Pursuit?

blocks.note: to mug is to rob, and the 's stands for is, written as S
someone game is willing, up for anything

explanation.surface: Asks whether a thief is keen on a round of the board game Trivial Pursuit.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make it look like the trivia board game, but read as lower case it is any pointless pursuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug's game is an activity that is futile or unrewarding, a trivial pursuit only a fool would take on.

clue.text: Impatient artist gets on phone

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist
to ring is to phone someone

explanation.surface: A restless painter picks up the telephone to chase something up.
explanation.definitionFit: Raring, as in raring to go, describes someone eager and impatient to start.

clue.text: Signature tune — one's own?

blocks.note: first meaning: the tune that identifies a show or performer
second meaning, read as three words: a song about me, a number of one's own

explanation.walkthrough: The second half splits the answer as THE ME SONG, the song belonging to oneself; the question mark flags this playful respacing.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme song is the recurring music that identifies a programme, film or performer, just as a signature tune does.

clue.text: Leaders of Oval mourn England's ghastly Ashes — the last in a series

indicators.note: the leaders of a group of words are the letters at their fronts

blocks.note: first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: Cricket fans at the Oval grieve over England's dreadful performance in the final Test of an Ashes series.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground, and the Ashes is the Test series between England and Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, hence used for the end or last of anything.

clue.text: Novel about Irish lake and church captivates unknown actress

indicators.note: about means around, so the novel's title wraps the next pieces
to captivate is to take captive and hold, so the combined novel and church enclose the unknown

blocks.note: She is the novel by H. Rider Haggard
IR is the abbreviation for Irish
L is the abbreviation for lake
algebra's unknowns are x, y and z
a temple is a place of worship

explanation.surface: A book about an Irish lough and its church enthrals some obscure performer.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two wrappings: the novel's title closes around the Irish lake, and then the novel together with the church holds the unknown between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Shirley Temple was the Hollywood child star of the 1930s, later a US diplomat.

clue.text: Means to turn and flee when tigers head off crazily

indicators.note: taking the head off a word removes its first letter
acting crazily means behaving wildly, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written; its first letter goes
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to wheel round and run as tigers charge wildly at you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' looks like a plea to intercept the tigers, but it beheads the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A steering wheel is the device a driver uses to turn a vehicle.

clue.text: Warning there's a lot of suffering about Rod's heavy drinking

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: harm is hurt or suffering; its last letter goes
a binge is a bout of heavy drinking
R is a recognised abbreviation for rod, an old unit of length

explanation.surface: A cautionary tale: a man called Rod's boozing will bring much misery.
explanation.walkthrough: The R comes after BINGE in the answer, so 'about' here only loosely joins the pieces rather than wrapping anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbinger is a forerunner that signals something to come, so it serves as a warning or omen.

clue.text: Last in the opening race

indicators.note: the last in a word is its final letter

blocks.note: final letter of the word
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: A runner who trails in the first heat of a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A race is a single contest in an athletics meeting, called an event.

clue.text: Succeed in getting to open water

blocks.note: first meaning: arrive at a place or goal
second meaning: a straight stretch of a river or sea

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one sentence about arriving at the sea, but splits into a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach somewhere is to arrive there, and a reach is also an uninterrupted expanse of river between bends.

clue.text: After strong drink Queen gets seized by wind — weaker one required!

indicators.note: after puts the following pieces behind the strong drink, which leads the answer
something seized by another is gripped inside it

blocks.note: gin is a strong spirit
a gale is a strong wind
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: After a stiff drink, Her Majesty is overcome by flatulence and needs something milder.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger ale is a soft, non-alcoholic mixer, much weaker than the gin that precedes it.

clue.text: What a dance

blocks.note: first meaning: a polite request to repeat something, as when saying 'What?'
second meaning: a dance where one may cut in and take another's partner

explanation.walkthrough: It looks like an exclamation of delight at a dance; in fact 'What' is one meaning and 'a dance' another.
explanation.definitionFit: Excuse me can be said to ask someone to repeat themselves, and it names a ballroom dance with partner changing.

clue.text: Horrible person squeezes Pledge on King's ornamental tassel

indicators.note: to squeeze something in is to press it into the middle

blocks.note: snot is slang for a nasty, contemptible person
giving your word is a pledge
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A nasty character forces a vow upon the monarch's decorative trimming.
explanation.definitionFit: A sword knot is a ribbon or tassel tied to a sword hilt as decoration.

clue.text: Big box? Not in this Japanese practice

definitions.text: Big box? Not in this Japanese practice

blocks.note: surface reading: a large container
setter's reading: box is also a shrub, and in this Japanese art trees are kept tiny

explanation.walkthrough: Box is a hedge shrub as well as a container; the Japanese art grows such plants in miniature, so no big box.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Japanese art of cultivating dwarf trees and shrubs in small pots.

clue.text: Sniper who shot Onassis?

indicators.note: something shot is wrecked or broken, so the letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: the fodder

explanation.surface: Asks which gunman fired at Onassis, recalling the Kennedy assassination and Jackie's later husband.
explanation.walkthrough: The Onassis meant is Aristotle, the Greek shipping tycoon, not Jackie; the question mark marks him as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle Onassis made his fortune owning a huge fleet of tankers and cargo vessels.

clue.text: Oddly this butter is used primarily for a dessert

indicators.note: oddly picks the letters in odd-numbered positions
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: first and third letters
a ram butts with its head, so it is a butter
taken as written
first letter

explanation.surface: A cook remarks that this particular butter is, strangely, mainly destined for a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' is not the dairy spread but one who butts, a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian dessert of coffee-soaked sponge layered with mascarpone.

clue.text: Money prize is worthless

blocks.note: tin is old slang for money
a pot is a trophy or prize

explanation.surface: A cynic dismissing a cash award as meaningless.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinpot describes something cheap, inferior and of little value, as in a tinpot dictator.

clue.text: Turn round German party in Chicago, perhaps

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the turn wraps the next piece

blocks.note: a winding is a turn or bend
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A German celebration in Chicago with a twist, like a spin round the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn round' looks like one phrasal verb; 'Turn' gives the outer word and 'round' wraps it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wingding is American slang for a lively party or celebration, so a Chicago example fits.

clue.text: One escapes from whole sheep's heart as a dish

indicators.note: whatever escapes from a word leaves it, so that letter is removed
the heart of a word is its central letter

blocks.note: entire means whole
I is the Roman numeral one, and it is removed
the central letter

explanation.surface: A sheep's heart served whole as a meal after one lamb gets away.
explanation.definitionFit: An entree is a dish served at a meal: a starter in Britain, a main course in North America.

clue.text: Country club bordering Iowa entertaining academic

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in and hold them inside

blocks.note: a mace is a spiked club
a don is a university teacher
IA is the postal abbreviation for Iowa

explanation.surface: A rural golf club near the Iowa state line hosts a university lecturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country club' looks like one phrase; the first word is the definition and 'club' starts the wordplay. The club and Iowa sit side by side and take the academic between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Macedonia, now North Macedonia, is a country in the Balkans.

clue.text: Company well-informed about fur

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the word for well-informed is read backwards

blocks.note: COY is the military abbreviation for a company
to be up on a subject is to be well-informed about it

explanation.surface: A business that knows all about the fur trade.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu is a South American rodent farmed for its fur, sold as nutria.

clue.text: Mug on hot rag

blocks.note: a mug and a clot are both a fool
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A coffee cup set down on a warm dishcloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' suggests a cup, but it means a fool; a clot is British slang for a stupid person.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag is a piece of old cloth, so cloth stands in for it as material.

clue.text: Greek characters leave wine for novice

indicators.note: letters that leave a word depart from it and are taken away

blocks.note: mu is the Greek letter M, and more than one are mus
Muscadet is a dry white wine from the Loire

explanation.surface: Some Greeks give up their wine in favour of a newcomer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a trainee in the armed forces or police, a beginner or novice.

clue.text: Endlessly using toy store?

indicators.note: endlessly means without ends, so first and last letters are cut away

blocks.note: using a toy is playing

explanation.surface: A child forever amusing itself in a toy shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Store' looks like a noun for a shop, but it is the verb meaning stock up.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay in supplies is to stock up on them for future use.

clue.text: Steps taken to avoid drought?

blocks.note: surface reading: measures such as water rationing to prevent a dry spell
setter's reading: literal dance steps performed in a ritual to summon wet weather

explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps' reads as measures or precautions, but literally they are footwork in a ritual dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A ritual dance performed to bring rain, as practised by some Native American peoples.

clue.text: Censor the hot stuff to pass inspection

blocks.note: a censor cuts material
taken as written
mustard is a hot condiment

explanation.surface: An instruction to remove racy content so a film gets past the regulator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot stuff' suggests something racy, but here it is a spicy condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut the mustard is an idiom for coming up to the required standard.
